title: Working as a lifeboat volunteer
subject: listening

paragraphs.text: I never really planned to be a lifeboat volunteer when I came to live in Northsea.
I’d been working in London as a website designer, but although that was interesting, I didn’t like city life.
I’d been really keen on boats as a teenager, and I thought if I went to live by the sea, I might be able to pursue that interest a bit more in my free time.
Then I found that the Lifeboat Institution was looking for volunteers, so I decided to apply.
The Lifeboat Institution building here in Northsea’s hard to miss, it’s one of the largest in the country.
It was built 15 years ago with funds provided by a generous member of the public who’d lived here all her life.
As the Lifeboat Institution is a charity that relies on that kind of donation, rather than funding provided by the government, that was a huge help to us.
When I applied, I had to have a health assessment. The doctors were particularly interested in my vision.
I used to be short-sighted, so I’d had to wear glasses, but I’d had laser eye surgery two years earlier so that was OK.
They gave me tests for colour blindness and they thought I might have a problem there, but it turned out I was OK.
When the coastguard gets an alert, all the volunteers are contacted and rush to the lifeboat station.
Our target’s to get there in five minutes, then we try to get the boat off the dock and out to sea in another six to eight minutes.
Our team’s proud that we usually achieve that – the average time across the country’s eight and a half minutes.
I’ve recently qualified as what’s called a ‘helmsman’, which means I have the ultimate responsibility for the lifeboat.
I have to check that the equipment we use is in working order – the crew have special life jackets that can support up to four people in the water.
And it’s ultimately my decision whether it’s safe to launch the boat.
But it’s very rare not to launch it, even in the worst weather.
As well as going out on the lifeboat, my work involves other things too.

A lot of people underestimate how quickly conditions can change at sea, so I speak to youth groups and sailing clubs in the area about the sorts of problems that sailors and swimmers can have if the weather suddenly gets bad.
We also have a lot of volunteers who organise activities to raise money for us, and we couldn’t manage without them.
The training we get is a continuous process, focusing on technical competence and safe handling techniques, and it’s given me the confidence to deal with extreme situations without panicking.
I was glad I’d done a first aid course before I started, as that’s a big help with the casualty care activities we do.
We’ve done a lot on how to deal with ropes and tie knots –that’s an essential skill.
After a year, I did a one-week residential course, led by specialists.
They had a wave-tank where they could create extreme weather conditions – so we could get experience at what to do if the boat turned over in a storm at night, for example.
Since I started, I’ve had to deal with a range of emergency situations.But the work’s hugely motivating.
It’s not just about saving lives – I’ve learned a lot about the technology involved.
My background in IT’s been useful here, and I can use my expertise to help other volunteers.
They’re a great group – we’re like a family really, which helps when you’re dragging yourself out of bed on a cold stormy night.
But actually, it’s the colder months that can be the most rewarding time. T
hat’s when the incidents tend to be more serious, and you realise that you can make a huge difference to the outcome.
So if any of you listeners are interested. . . .

groups.instruction:
Questions 11–16

Choose the correct letter, A, B or C.

Working as a lifeboat volunteer

questions.prompt: What made David leave London and move to Northsea?

options.text: He was eager to develop a hobby.
He wanted to work shorter hours.
He found his job in website design unsatisfying.

questions.explanation: 题干要求选出David离开伦敦搬到Northsea的原因。原文中，David首先提到自己working in London as a website designer，但随后说到that was interesting，可否定C选项。随后提到自己从小喜欢船，如果搬到海边，能够pursue that interest a bit more in my free time。A选项中的hobby为interest的同义替换，该选项正确。B选项意为“想要缩短工作时长”，在原文中没有提及。

questions.prompt: The Lifeboat Institution in Northsea was built with money provided by

options.text: a local organisation.
a local resident.
the local council.

questions.explanation: 题干要求选出救生艇协会建造的资金来源。题干中的money在原文中替换为funds，后文出现a generous member of the public who lived here all her life，替换了B选项的local resident，需要考生对原文长句有充分理解并且识别替换。A选项的local organisation原文没有提及。C选项的local council在原文中出现了近义词government，但rather than提示并非政府出资，并且此处描述的是协会目前运作的情况，并非建造时的资金来源，和题干要求也不符。

questions.prompt: In his health assessment, the doctor was concerned about the fact that David

options.text: might be colour blind.
was rather short-sighted.
had undergone eye surgery.

questions.explanation: 题干中的health assessment原词重现。原文首先出现了B选项的short-sighted，但used to说明目前已没有这个问题，随后的I’d had laser eye surgery也可提示排除B选项。同时，此句也出现了C选项的关键词eye surgery，但原文并没有提到这是医生关注的事情，故排除C选项。下一句中的colour blindness对应A选项，they thought I might have a problem here对应题干中的the doctor was concerned about，因此可确定答案为A选项。

questions.prompt: After arriving at the lifeboat station, they aim to launch the boat within

options.text: five minutes.
six to eight minutes.
eight and a half minutes.

questions.explanation: 题干问的是志愿者到达救生艇码头后的目标是在多长时间内放船下水。原文首先出现A选项的five minutes，但此处为到达lifeboat station的时间，和题干不符。下一句中try to get the boat off the dock and out to sea替换了题干中的aim to launch the boat，需要考生理解launch此处的含义“使（船）下水”，并识别原文替换。随后出现答案six to eight minutes，对应B选项。下一句的eight and a half minutes为该国的平均时长，与题干要求不符。

questions.prompt: As a ‘helmsman’, David has the responsibility of deciding

options.text: who will be the members of his crew.
what equipment it will be necessary to take.
if the lifeboat should be launched.

questions.explanation: 本题需选出David负责决定什么事情。原文首先出现B选项原词equipment，但原文为check that the equipment we use is in working order，即“检查设备是否正常运作”，而不是B选项中的“检查需要带哪些设备”。下一句中出现A选项原词crew，但原文为描述crew有特殊的救生衣，并非说话人要决定带哪些船员。最后出现it’s ultimately my decision whether it’s safe to launch the boat，对应C选项，注意C选项中的if意为“是否”，和原文的whether功能相同，引导宾语从句。此处请参照前文“文本解析”第三句的翻译。

questions.prompt: As well as going out on the lifeboat, David

options.text: gives talks on safety at sea.
helps with fundraising.
recruits new volunteers.

questions.explanation: 题干中的As well as going out on the lifeboat在原文中重现。原文下一句出现speak to youth groups and sailing clubs，对应A选项的give talks；原文中about后谈到演讲内容是“sorts of problems that…if the weather suddenly gets bad”，对应A选项的safety at sea。接下来一句提到raise money，对应B选项的fundraising，但本句中的“We also have a lot of volunteers…and we couldn’t manage without them”说明筹款活动为志愿者们所做，并非说话人所做，故排除B选项。C选项的“招募新志愿者”并未提及。

groups.instruction:
Questions 17 and 18

Choose TWO letters, A–E.

questions.prompt: Which TWO things does David say about the lifeboat volunteer training?

options.text: The residential course developed his leadership skills.
The training in use of ropes and knots was quite brief.
The training exercises have built up his mental strength.
The casualty care activities were particularly challenging for him.
The wave tank activities provided practice in survival techniques.

questions.explanation: 本题需要选出David关于救生艇志愿者培训所说的两方面内容。原文首先提到it’s given me the confidence to deal with extreme situations without panicking，对应C选项的have built up his mental strength，该选项为正确答案之一。需要考生理解confidence和without panicking的含义。下一句出现D选项的casualty care activities，但未提及challenging。B选项的ropes和knots原词出现，但原文We’ve done a lot和选项中brief不符。接下来出现A选项的residential course，但原文仅提到专家授课，并未提及leadership。随后出现E选项的wave tank，后文get experience at what to do if the boat turned over in a storm at night即选项中的practice in survival techniques，因此可确定E选项为另一个正确答案。此处原文为具体例子，选项则较为概括抽象，需要考生具备一定的理解能力和概括能力。

It was built 15 years ago with funds provided by a generous member of the public who’d lived here all her life.

I used to be short-sighted, so I’d had to wear glasses, but I’d had laser eye surgery two years earlier so that was OK.

Our team’s proud that we usually achieve that – the average time across the country’s eight and a half minutes.
